routing_warnings.description: The separate proposal to provide Danish style names concerns the style-naming Requirement rather than default document-language configuration.
The Danish wording proposal concerns Word style names rather than user-facing field labels or placeholders.
The requirement that fields remain unique and not repeat content concerns field independence rather than Danish wording.
Requiring every interactive field to have a control label concerns label availability and behavior rather than localization.
Matching labels to initial field text and recovering the field purpose on hover concerns persistent help behavior.
Displaying help text in both the label and field concerns help-text placement rather than Danish wording.
Keeping help text available after a field is emptied concerns persistence behavior.
Keeping visible in-field help text and permitting duplication with the label concerns help-text visibility and placement.
This message specifies the bullet-list visual design rather than general style-catalog completeness.
The reported break after the eighth bullet concerns list hierarchy behavior rather than catalog availability.
This failure arose from Tab-key list-level behavior and is better routed to the list-hierarchy Requirement.
The requested caption-text style name belongs to the independently defined caption-style Requirement.
The absence of the caption style directly concerns the caption-style Requirement.
The requested name "caption text" applies specifically to the image and table caption style, for which the inventory contains a narrower Requirement.
The reported break after the eighth bullet concerns list-level hierarchy behavior rather than bullet visual rendering.
The freelancer's concern is whether users invoke list levels with Tab instead of the style ribbon, which concerns hierarchy behavior rather than the bullet design itself.
The report that the list breaks after the eighth bullet appears to concern list-level hierarchy rather than alignment of multi-digit numbering.
The missing green bullet at level 9 concerns bullet appearance rather than multi-digit numbered-list alignment.
The client explicitly attributes the observed list behavior to using the Tab key without changing styles, making list hierarchy the better target.
The inability to use Enter in an ordinary text area concerns multiline field input, not automatic bullet creation.
This message concerns automatic numbering during Board Meeting row or field entry rather than bullet continuation in the Board Recommendation control.
The pasted-table shift is a table-containment failure rather than evidence about general pasted-content style stability.

The request to reduce spacing so the document fits within three pages belongs to the separate page-fit Requirement; only the reported successful legacy-content paste applies to the target Requirement.
The successful legacy-content paste report concerns general formatting stability and does not specifically verify pasted table or column containment.
The right-hand column is pushed outward because text in interactive fields does not wrap; this is field text-wrapping behavior rather than pasted-table containment.
The report that Master Template tables are not working concerns table operability in that template, not containment after pasting.
The hard-return spacing issue concerns continuous text in interactive fields, not manual line breaks after legacy-content pasting.
The inability to use Enter in the current interactive text area concerns multiline field input rather than post-paste line breaks.
The distinction between standard Enter and Shift+Enter concerns multiline field input rather than post-paste behavior.
The remaining Enter failure is localized to an interactive field area and does not identify a legacy-paste workflow.
The claim that Enter is working everywhere addresses the interactive-field issue discussed immediately beforehand, not post-paste line breaks.
The request for Danish label text changes localization rather than the label-and-help mechanism.
The specified Danish date placeholder belongs to user-facing text localization.
The specified Danish subject placeholder belongs to user-facing text localization.
This message asks whether existing field text clears automatically upon activation.
This message reports that existing field text does not clear automatically.
The field-related clauses report automatic-clearing failures rather than label or persistent-help behavior.
This runtime failure concerns automatic field clearing.
The request to fix the inappropriate legacy-field setup concerns the underlying field implementation architecture rather than visual discoverability alone.
The excessive spacing produced by hard returns is a paragraph-spacing behavior separate from whether standard Enter is accepted in multiline fields.
Automatic numbered-row creation when Enter is pressed concerns the Board Meeting row-insertion workflow rather than ordinary multiline field input.
The requested Danish date-field placeholder concerns user-facing text rather than the reusable date-entry mechanism.
This message clarifies Danish placeholder text and should be routed to the localization Requirement.
Regular Enter input is an independently tracked multiline-input behavior rather than an attribute of the date-control mechanism.
The opening clause separately verifies that content copied from the old document looks correct; that observation belongs to legacy-content paste stability rather than page fit.
The excessive spacing described here concerns hard returns in continuous text, which is narrower than overall document density and page fit.
The 0.18 row and column spacing claim addresses local text-to-border padding rather than overall document page fit.
The concrete failure concerns Enter-key input in a field; the accompanying spacing question depends on the local padding exchange and does not establish an overall page-fit event.
The first clause reports a separate Enter-key failure in the last field area.
The margin-collapse claim concerns fixed-margin behavior rather than right-side text padding.
The claim that Enter works everywhere concerns multiline field input rather than text-to-border padding.
The request concerns spacing between text and the right-hand border, not paragraph-return spacing.
The observed failure concerns whether standard Enter can be used in a field, not the spacing produced by a successful return.
The concrete failure is that Enter still does not work in one field; the accompanying spacing question does not clearly identify paragraph-return spacing.
The explicit implementation claim says Enter is working everywhere; its generic top-and-bottom spacing statement does not clearly entail a fix for continuous-text return spacing.
The headline-field failure concerns availability of Enter input rather than the visual spacing produced by a return.
The clause about Item and Title not aligning with Topic, Proposal, and Start Time belongs to the independent Board Meeting field-alignment Requirement.
The request to reuse Board Seminar date functionality in the Board Meeting template belongs to the reusable date-control Requirement.
The reported break after the eighth bullet is a concrete list-hierarchy failure, not evidence about the general Windows operating environment.
The successful legacy-content paste observation belongs to the independently testable paste-stability Requirement.
The Master Template element failures are narrower product-behavior failures and should not be absorbed into the broad Windows compatibility Requirement.
The reported text duplication is a failure of the dedicated Master Template text-duplication Requirement.
The report that the tables are not working is a failure of the dedicated Master Template table-operability Requirement.
The table shifting reported here occurs during legacy-content pasting and belongs to pasted-table containment rather than ordinary Master Template table operation.
The separate clause stating that the tables are not working belongs to the Master Template Table Operability Requirement.
The clauses about user-added bullet counts, highlighted bullet content, automatic text shrinking, and preserving grid relationships concern the independently defined dynamic bullet-layout behavior.
The content-box resizing and manual-layout alternative concern dynamic content accommodation rather than faithful implementation of the static customer-designed slide system.
The Heading 3 boldness clause belongs to the separately inventoried Heading 3 typography Requirement.
The multi-digit list-alignment failure belongs to the numbered-list alignment Requirement.
This message clarifies that Overskrift 3 means Heading 3 and therefore supports the separate Heading 3 Requirement.
Delivery of a template containing every style is a catalog-level implementation claim and does not specifically identify Title typography.
The concrete reported failure concerns the bullet hierarchy after level eight, not Title typography.
Loss of formatting when interacting with the Title field concerns interactive-field formatting preservation rather than the approved Title typography value.
The separate clause reporting broken alignment at list number 10 belongs to the numbered-list alignment Requirement.
This message concerns title and Heading 1 typography, not Heading 3.
